description: brainstorm-toolkit — surface the .next-action seam + keep long loops context-cheap. Three Stop hooks (they run in PARALLEL; array order is documentation only, not precedence). next-action.sh surfaces /brainstorm handoffs, /sdlc --queue park-resumes, and gotcha seams as `Next: …` (and, with pipeline.auto_continue, drives the loop). The SessionStart hook (matcher compact|clear) reseeds a pointer to the loop's durable on-disk state after a compaction/clear, so aggressive auto-compaction stays lossless for the orchestrator. Merges with any user/project hooks (deduped by command). `run-cost-report.sh` fires once per run, when a pipeline envelope reaches a terminal status (complete/failed/paused): it reads the hook's own transcript_path and prints turns, average context, peak, cache-read and rough spend. It is emitted as `systemMessage`, so it reaches the HUMAN watching the terminal and never enters the model's context -- that is what makes it free, and it is also why it is only seen if someone is looking (never switch it to hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext). It never blocks and never resets (no tool can force /clear or /compact). Silence it with project.json pipeline.context.cost_report set to off. The earlier mid-run threshold nag and its pipeline.context.warn_above_tokens knob were removed -- see docs/LOOP-HYGIENE.md for why a lagging mid-run warning was the wrong shape. See docs/SEAM.md and docs/LOOP-HYGIENE.md. `stop-gate.sh` is inert unless project.json sets pipeline.stop_gate: "tests" AND an /sdlc run's envelope is in_progress AND test.unit is configured; then a red test.unit run returns decision:block (bounded by pipeline.loop.max_hops) instead of letting the run hand off silently red. It guarantees by construction that it is never a second blocker: it stands down (no output at all when the gate itself is off) whenever project.json sets pipeline.loop.auto_continue: true (the primary guard -- next-action.sh can only block from inside that same knob, so this makes the two mutually exclusive by CONFIG, which no interleaving can defeat), and secondarily whenever stdin's stop_hook_active is true or a .next-action sentinel is pending -- next-action.sh owns the block in that event. See docs/SEAM.md. `enforce-model-cap.sh` is a PreToolUse(Agent) hook, inert unless project.json sets pipeline.enforce_cap: true; then it rewrites a dispatch `model` above models.cap down to the cap (and sets it when omitted, unless the agent definition pins one), exempting Axis 2 dispatches whose description starts `review:`. Reports each rewrite as systemMessage. Never blocks.
